$comment: Regression ceilings in gzipped bytes, checked by scripts/verify-package.mjs through .github/scripts/size-budget.mjs. Size is not a target: each ceiling sits about 15-20% above what was measured when it was set, to catch an accidental blow-up. Raise one on purpose, in the pull request that needs it, and update its reason.

..reason: Raised 2026-09-25 with the calendar part dimension (N2), about 17% over the 119,245 B measured then: the kernel has grown by the descriptor narrowing (N5) and the chart families (D41) since the ceiling was set, and N1, N3 and N4 add to the same kernel next.

./react.reason: Raised 2026-09-25 with the time between two moments (N3), about 17% over the 146,099 B measured then: the editor controllers carry the kernel's rules for calendar parts (N2), opening and closing values (N1) and durations (N3) since the ceiling was set.

./ui.reason: Raised 2026-09-26 after a board's date filter showing what the board reads (#3619) took ./ui to 616,466 B, 466 B over the old ceiling; about 17% over that measurement. The growth is the intended feature, not a bundling accident.

echarts chunk.reason: Set 2026-09-25, about 17% over the 528 B measured then. The chunk /ui loads by import() on a chart's first use; echarts itself is external, bundled by the host.

./styles.css.reason: Raised 2026-09-25 with the theme's role tier (S3: the roles' declarations and their data-slot rules), about 17% over the 30,297 B measured then.

./themes.css.reason: Set 2026-09-25, about 18% over the 2,888 B measured once slate, graphite and fjord were removed (five presets). The themes design budget (8 KB, themes.md 5.6) still holds beside it.
